headline: Authors report that rare training facts raise LLM discovery rates in two controlled scientific domains
summary: A 2 November 2026 preprint studies whether facts seen once in training are linked to language-model discovery capacity. In experiments on materials-science and regulatory-genomics tasks, the authors report that raising the share of these “monofacts” increases exact recovery of held-out target materials or DNA sequences across two open-weight model families. Repeated exposure weakens the trend while holding training-set diversity fixed. In-distribution, higher monofact rates also raise hallucinated outputs; cross-domain effects require in-domain training data. The results are author-reported and concern controlled target-recovery tasks, not prospective laboratory discoveries or broad scientific autonomy.
